name: Chapeau
classification_notes: Low-contrast geometric sans-serif with rounded terminals, drawn loosely from IBM's Doric – one of the few proportionally-aligned typewriter faces of the late 1960s. Simple geometric construction with careful width control produces an efficient, contemporary quality. Revised and expanded in 2016. Includes a matching mono subfamily.
summary: A low-contrast geometric sans-serif from Zurich-based Milieu Grotesque, rooted in IBM's rare Doric typewriter face and refined across six weights with a mono companion.
description: Designed by Timo Gaessner and first released in 2010, Chapeau takes its cue from IBM's Doric – one of the few proportionally-aligned typewriter faces of the late 1960s – distilling its geometric simplicity into a clean, low-contrast sans-serif with rounded terminals. The family spans six weights with matching italics and includes a mono variant, giving it genuine range across editorial, branding and UI contexts. Revised and expanded in 2016, it has appeared in Dazed and brand work for AIGA Eye on Design.
foundry_blurb: Milieu Grotesque is a Zurich-based type studio founded in 2010 by Timo Gaessner and Alexander Colby. The foundry maintains a small, tightly curated portfolio built around enduring, elegant type, and was acquired by Monotype in 2023.

name: Maison
classification_notes: Mono-lined constructivist grotesque grounded in early 20th-century Neue Sachlichkeit principles. Drawn with deliberate geometric rigidity and minimal optical correction — a property that distinguishes it from its descendant, Maison Neue. The family runs across proportional and monospaced alignments at matching weights, making it one of the few grotesques built from the outset to serve both roles without compromise.
summary: A rigid, mono-lined grotesque drawn for a Berlin architecture firm, rooted in Neue Sachlichkeit principles and built to run cleanly across proportional and monospaced alignments.
description: Maison was designed by Timo Gaessner as a corporate identity typeface for Thomas Bendel Architect, drawing its formal logic from early 20th-century constructivist grotesques. The construction is deliberately stiff: mono-lined strokes, minimal optical correction, letterforms built on a grid rather than tuned by eye. Five weights from Light to Bold are paired with matching italics and a parallel mono subfamily, making it one of the few grotesques conceived from the start to work in both proportional and fixed-width settings. Maison Neue, released two years later, softened these principles; the original holds its harder edge.
foundry_blurb: Milieu Grotesque was founded in Zurich in 2010 by graphic designers Timo Gaessner and Alexander Colby as a type platform for designers. The foundry produces a small, deliberate catalogue built on historical grotesk reference, with development cycles that typically run several years per release. It was acquired by Monotype in 2023.

name: Boutique
classification_notes: Built on a Didone skeleton with vertical axis and pronounced stroke contrast; geometric character amplified, ornament eliminated. Not a serif despite the Didone reference — it is a high-contrast sans-serif drawing on the skeletal logic of 18th-century moderns. Expanded in 2022 into a three-optical-size system (S, M, L) covering caption through display, with a serifed companion (Boutique Serif) and a dedicated italic (Boutique Italic). 54 styles total across the full family. Six upright weights per optical size.
summary: A high-contrast sans built on a Didone skeleton, expanded in 2022 into a 54-style system across three optical sizes with serifed and italic companions.
description: Originally a three-weight sans from 2012, Timo Gaessner rebuilt Boutique into a 54-style family a decade later, adding six weights across three optical sizes alongside a serifed companion and a dedicated italic. The underlying structure is Didone: vertical axis, sharp contrast, deliberate geometry, with decoration entirely absent. The result is an idiosyncratic reinterpretation of 18th-century moderns, sharpened for contemporary editorial and branding contexts.
foundry_blurb: Built on a Didone skeleton with its geometric character amplified and ornament eliminated, Boutique proposes an alternative present for the Modern typeface genre. Three optical sizes cover caption through display settings, and the full system includes a companion serif and a dedicated italic, creating a freely interchangeable typographic system.

name: Patron
classification_notes: An expressive grotesque that synthesises two opposing historical influences: the rigorous Swiss precision of Günther Gerhard Lange and the organic French warmth of Roger Excoffon. Distinctive features include angled, subtly flared terminals, a generous x-height and fairly small apertures. Geometric undertones provide structure while the flared strokes introduce character. The result sits between a classical grotesque and a personality-forward display sans.
summary: A luxury grotesque that fuses the rigorous precision of Günther Gerhard Lange with the organic warmth of Roger Excoffon, landing in refined, expressive territory.
description: Patron is a sans-serif family by Timo Gaessner built around the tension between two opposing design philosophies: Lange's Swiss exactitude and Excoffon's French sensibility. Large x-height, angled terminals and subtly flared strokes give it both legibility and presence. Across six weights with matching italics, it moves comfortably between editorial headlines, institutional identity and luxury fashion contexts.
foundry_blurb: Patron unites the contradictory approaches of Günther Gerhard Lange and Roger Excoffon to produce a versatile grotesque with a distinct visual language. Built for prominent roles across print and digital, it balances precise modern execution with an unconventional sense of balance — suited to everything from lookbooks to cultural institution branding.

name: Maison Neue
classification_notes: Neo-grotesque sans-serif redrawn from the earlier Maison typeface, moving away from geometric rigidity toward optically resolved letterforms guided by harmony, rhythm and flow. Closer in sensibility to mid-century European grotesques than strict Swiss rationalism. The 2017 superfamily expansion brought three widths – a subtly condensed standard, an extended counterpart and a mono-spaced variant – with five core weights plus additional cuts (two lighter, two heavier), and matching italics throughout. Cyrillic and Vietnamese support added October 2020. Now owned by Monotype.
summary: Timo Gaessner's 40-style neo-grotesque superfamily, redrawn from the original Maison with optical refinement as its governing principle – spanning standard, extended and mono widths across five weights with matching italics.
description: Maison Neue began as a typeface for a Berlin architectural practice before Gaessner expanded it into a 40-style superfamily for Milieu Grotesque, with the major revision landing in 2017. The redesign discarded the modular rigidity of the original Maison in favour of a more optically resolved grotesque – one shaped by attention to rhythm, harmony and flow. Three width variants cover standard, extended and mono settings, each carrying the full weight range with italics, with Cyrillic and Vietnamese support added in 2020.
foundry_blurb: Milieu Grotesque describes Maison Neue as a meticulous reworking of its predecessor – less formulaic in construction, guided by optical criteria over geometric dogma. The result spans condensed, extended and mono variants across 40 styles, built to carry a distinct visual language from editorial body text to display settings, analog print to digital UI.
